# Vault

[English](https://github.com/BlusteryS/Vault/blob/main/README.md) | [Русский](https://github.com/BlusteryS/Vault/blob/main/README_RU.md)

Vault is a standalone, multi-currency economy for Nukkit, Nukkit-MOT and Lumi. It stores balances itself and gives plugins one asynchronous API for money, points, donation currency and any currencies you add.

It can also replace an economy that is already in use. Vault imports its balances once, then emulates the old plugin name and API for plugins that still depend on it. EconomyAPI, Coins, playerPoints and OrynthEconomy profiles are included in the Vault jar.

## What you can do

- Run Vault as the only economy on a new server.
- Keep `money` and `coins` as separate currencies in the same database.
- Move balances from EconomyAPI, Coins, playerPoints or OrynthEconomy.
- Remove the old economy jar after migration and enable its compatibility profile.
- Enable several profiles together. For example, EconomyAPI can expose `money` while playerPoints exposes `coins`.
- Add `/money`, `/coins`, `/pay`, `/baltop`, `/setcoins` and similar commands from configuration.
- Use SQLite on one server or MySQL/PostgreSQL for shared balances.

Vault does not proxy live operations to installed economy plugins. After startup, every balance operation goes to Vault Ledger. Installed economies are only opened as migration sources when `/vault migrate` reads their data.

## Installation

1. Put `Vault.jar` in the `plugins` directory.
2. Start the server once.
3. Edit `plugins/Vault/ledger.yml` if you need different currencies or a network database.
4. Restart the server after changing Ledger or database settings.

The default setup creates two currencies:

- `money`, with two decimal places;
- `coins`, with whole-number balances.

SQLite is selected by default and needs no additional software.

## Configuration

Vault keeps unrelated settings in separate files:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `config.yml` | Configuration format version |
| `ledger.yml` | Database, performance and currencies |
| `commands.yml` | Optional commands and their messages |
| `emulation.yml` | Compatibility profiles |

### Add a currency

Add a section to `ledger.yml`:

```yaml
currencies:
  gems:
    enabled: true
    display-name: "Gems"
    symbol: "♦"
    role: DONATION
    scale: 0
    initial-balance: "0"
    maximum-balance: "1000000"
```

`scale` is the number of decimal places. Use `0` for whole points and `2` for conventional money. Restart the server after changing this file.

### Use MySQL or PostgreSQL

Select the database and fill in the existing `network` section:

```yaml
database:
  type: postgresql
  network:
    url: "jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/vault?sslmode=prefer&tcpKeepAlive=true"
    username: "vault"
    password: "replace-this"
    workers: 4
```

The same section accepts a `jdbc:mysql:` URL when `type` is `mysql`. Vault uses a bounded worker pool and does not run JDBC work on the server thread.

### Create commands without code

Every command in `commands.yml` chooses an operation and a Vault currency.

Example balance command:

```yaml
commands:
  coins:
    enabled: true
    type: balance
    currency: coins
    aliases: [coin, mycoins]
    description: "Show a coins balance"
    usage: "/coins [player]"
    permission: ""
    other-player-permission: "vault.command.coins.others"
    messages:
      self: "&eYour coins: &f{balance} {symbol}"
      other: "&e{target}'s coins: &f{balance} {symbol}"
      no-permission: "&cYou cannot view another player's balance."
      player-not-found: "&cPlayer {target} was not found."
      failure: "&cCannot read the balance: {status}"
```

Available command types are `balance`, `set`, `add`, `take`, `pay` and `top`. The supplied file contains complete examples for a balance, payment, leaderboard and administration command.

## Migration

Keep the old economy installed during migration. Vault detects supported plugins and lists them in `/vault status` or `/vault migrate`.

Command format:

```text
/vault migrate <source> <source-currency> <target-currency>
```

Examples:

```text
/vault migrate economyapi default money
/vault migrate playerpoints points coins
/vault migrate oryntheconomy regular money
/vault migrate oryntheconomy donate coins
```

The first run shows a preview. Repeat the command with `confirm` to start:

```text
/vault migrate economyapi default money confirm
```

Vault clears the target currency, reads the source in stable pages and writes every balance to Ledger. It never changes the source. Stop shops, rewards and other balance writers until the command finishes.

After checking the imported balances:

1. stop the server;
2. remove the old economy jar;
3. enable emulation if another plugin still declares the old economy as a dependency;
4. start the server again.

Custom economy plugins can provide a migration source through the [migration SPI](https://github.com/BlusteryS/Vault/blob/main/docs/API.md#migration-spi).

## Emulation

Emulation loads a small compatibility plugin directly from the Vault jar. It does not create another jar and does not keep a second balance store.

Example: provide EconomyAPI and playerPoints at the same time:

```yaml
profiles:
  economy-api:
    enabled: true
    profile: classic-2.0
    currencies:
      default: money

  player-points:
    enabled: true
    profile: current
    currencies:
      default: coins
```

Example: replace OrynthEconomy:

```yaml
profiles:
  orynth-economy:
    enabled: true
    profile: current
    currencies:
      regular: money
      donate: coins
```

EconomyAPI has two profiles:

- `classic-2.0` for the common single-currency API;
- `mot-2.1` for the Nukkit-MOT multi-currency API.

A real plugin and its emulated profile cannot be loaded together.

## Plugin API

All modern operations are asynchronous and use `BigDecimal`.

```java
EconomyClient economy = Vault.client(this);

economy.withdraw(player, "money", new BigDecimal("25.00"))
    .thenAccept(result -> {
        if (!result.success()) {
            getLogger().warning("Payment failed: " + result.status());
            return;
        }

        BigDecimal balance = result.balanceAfter().orElseThrow();
        Vault.mainThreadExecutor().execute(() ->
            player.sendMessage("Balance: " + balance)
        );
    })
    .exceptionally(error -> {
        getLogger().error("Cannot access Vault Ledger", error);
        return null;
    });
```

The API supports online players, offline accounts by UUID, system accounts, transfers, leaderboards, full currency resets, currency creation and idempotent mutations. See the complete [API documentation](https://github.com/BlusteryS/Vault/blob/main/docs/API.md).

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/vault status` | Database, currencies, emulation and migration sources |
| `/vault reload` | Reload `commands.yml` and `emulation.yml` |
| `/vault reset <currency> [confirm]` | Wipe one currency |
| `/vault migrate ...` | List sources or import balances |

Ledger and database changes require a server restart.

## Building

```bash
./gradlew clean build
```

The server plugin is written to `vault-plugin/build/libs/Vault-<version>.jar`.
